# Tabsona

> Give each Chrome tab its own login session. Save, open and reuse a whole set of signed-in sites as a persona. A Manifest V3 extension for developers testing their own apps across many roles and tenants.

Tabsona isolates logins per tab inside one Chrome window. A **persona** is an identity across a set of apps and holds at most one saved login per site; opening a persona opens every site as a tab, each already signed in.

It works by combining two Chrome APIs that cannot do each other's job: `declarativeNetRequest` session rules replace the `Cookie` header per tab (and strip `Set-Cookie` from responses so the browser's own jar never learns the login), while observational `webRequest` reads the raw `Set-Cookie` — HttpOnly included — to capture it into the session. Page storage is isolated by a MAIN-world shim that namespaces `localStorage` keys by **session id**, which is what makes saving and restoring a session possible at all.

It is not an anti-detect browser. Fingerprint spoofing, proxy-per-session, ban evasion and cloud sync are out of scope by design.

## Docs

- [How it works](https://github.com/khanakia/tabsona/blob/main/docs/how-it-works.md): the model, the exact Chrome APIs, the four ways to build a session, and the architecture
- [README](https://github.com/khanakia/tabsona/blob/main/README.md): install, usage, keyboard shortcuts, verification
- [Limits](https://github.com/khanakia/tabsona/blob/main/docs/limits.md): every known hole, each marked verified-in-code or assumed
- [Contributing](https://github.com/khanakia/tabsona/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md): the two rules the project is built around, and the gate
- [Security](https://github.com/khanakia/tabsona/blob/main/SECURITY.md): what it stores, where, and how to report a vulnerability

## Known limitations

- Service-worker fetches carry no tab id, so they bypass per-tab isolation. Unfixable in the extension model.
- IndexedDB is detected and reported as leaking, not isolated.
- Partitioned cookies (CHIPS) are modelled but not captured.
- Cross-origin iframes cannot learn which session they belong to.
